publicReleaseNotes: A healthy check by the Worker writes 2 database rows instead of 6, so Workers Free's 100,000 rows written a day go about three times as far. A check that passes with nothing to report no longer writes a history row of its own; it is kept with the monitor's availability record and reads everywhere as before: in history, the overview, reports, the read API, exports and erasure receipts. Local measurements for eight one-minute monitors: about 24,500 rows written a day while healthy (70,600 before). Slow and Slow recovered notices fire again for monitors checked by the Worker. No database migrations. Rollback to 0.5.39 is safe: it already reads such checks. Do not roll back to 0.5.38 or earlier once this release has run. Product screenshot available from Uptime 0.4.0 at 1440 pixels (.github/assets/release/uptime-0.4.0-monitor-1440.png). — Run Edit Run fleet, 2026-11-27
